title: Flexible Pay and Labor Supply: Evidence from Uber's Instant Pay
eligible_reason: Randomized controlled trial analyzed without unit or treatment-group fixed effects, so no reported specification is a two-way fixed-effects DiD. Every regression absorbs city_x_cohort_x_day (128 occurrences) or city_x_cohort (42, Appendix Table 5) and never driver_uuid; the single regressor is treated_x_post3w (treated driver x at least 3 weeks after cohort enrollment). Without driver or treated-group FE the treated drivers' level difference is identified only by randomization within city-cohort cells, which is an ITT regression with strata-by-day FE rather than Hull's alpha_i + lambda_t + beta D_it model. The headline estimator is also Poisson (ppmlhdfe, Table 1 columns 1-4); OLS versions (columns 5-8) share the FE structure. Staggered enrollment exists (cohorts enrolled on different dates, Appendix Table 8), but it is handled by cohort-by-day FE, not by a staggered TWFE comparison.
design_notes: Driver-day panel (instantpay_clean.dta, 2.4 GB) of Uber drivers in the Instant Pay RCT, January-April 2016. treated = RCT arm; post_3w = at least 21 days after driver-specific enrollment date (city cohorts enrolled on different dates); treated_x_post3w = product. Table 1 (3-InstantPay_Analysis.do lines 150-195): ppmlhdfe / reghdfe {session_length_minutes, session_earnings, any_sessions, session_length_minutes if any_sessions==1} treated_x_post3w, vce(cluster driver_uuid) absorb(city_x_cohort_x_day). Figure 2 varies the post cutoff; Figure 3 heterogeneity splits; Figure 4 / Table 3 interact with day-of-week; Appendix Table 3 IV (applied = treated); Appendix Table 5 absorb(city_x_cohort) with post_3w main effect; Appendix Figure B1 leads/lags treated_x_lag8w..treated_x_lead7w with city_x_cohort_x_day FE (Poisson). Orange County experiment (Appendix C) is a separate RCT.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Multiple enrollment cohorts (variable cohort; Appendix Table 8 lists modal start dates per city), but no specification uses unit FE; a TWFE version would require adding driver_uuid FE, which the paper does not report.

specs.exclusion_reason: no unit or treatment-group fixed effects (city_x_cohort_x_day FE only); RCT ITT regression
specs.outcome: session_length_minutes (columns 6-8: session_earnings, any_sessions, minutes if any_sessions==1)
specs.treatment_definition: treated (Instant Pay arm) x post_3w (>= 3 weeks after the driver's enrollment date; cohort-specific)
specs.notes: Adding driver FE would yield a staggered TWFE with cohort-by-day FE, but that is not a reported specification.

data_access: partial (anonymized driver-day analysis files shipped; raw trip-level Uber data proprietary and not shared)
data_files_note: README: driver IDs are re-coded ('synthetic driver ID created for this replication package') but the data are the real anonymized driver-day panel; raw Data-Extract files are not shipped.
software_notes: Stata 18 MP (reghdfe, ppmlhdfe, ivreghdfe, estout, iebaltab); analysis do-file takes about 7 hours.
priority_note: Not a TWFE design as reported.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text). absorb() patterns enumerated with grep over 3-InstantPay_Analysis.do: city_x_cohort_x_day (128), city_x_cohort (42), date_local (1); no driver FE anywhere. If the team decides RCTs with strata-by-day FE count as group-FE designs, revisit: treated_x_post3w with cohort-specific onset would then be a candidate with 'treated' main effect absorbed only by randomization.
